Thanks — Thu 4/9 11:00 PT confirmed. A couple of quick clarifications ahead of the call so we can prioritize:

1) Key management: HydraHealth prefers customer-managed keys (KMS) for PHI-adjacent projects — can you confirm whether that is supported for Private deployments and what the timelines look like?
2) Logging: we'll want to see a sample of structured access logs (JSON) and an example of how prefix/KV cache information appears in logs so our engineers can validate retention boundaries.
3) Data residency: if we start in Redwood Hosted US region, what are options to move to a VPC/private deployment later? Any expected downtime or migration windows?

I've uploaded a focused question subset to the Drive folder (link below). If you can point to specific attachments during the call that would help us move quickly.

Date: Wed, 8 Apr 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ request + scheduling a short walkthrough — call recap and action items

Elena — thanks for the call today. Summary and agreed next steps below.

Meeting notes (Thu 4/9 11:00 PT):
- Attendees: Elena Torres (HydraHealth), security@hydrahealth.com, Olga Petrov (Redwood), Ben Carter (Redwood), Monica Patel (Redwood)
- Duration: 39 minutes
- High-level: Walked through CAIQ sections mapped to SOC 2 controls. Confirmed most baseline controls are covered by Redwood's SOC 2 (Scope: storage, API, control plane). Discussed timeline and artifacts for Private deployment KMS options.

Agreed action items and owners:
1) Monica: upload sample logging export (sample-logging-export-202603.zip) and add a short readme explaining fields (ETA: Fri 4/10 EOD).
2) Olga: share CAIQ->SOC2 mapping slide and redwood_architecture_diagram_v2.png with the Hydra team (ETA: Fri 4/10 noon PT).
3) Ben: start contract thread for KMS addendum and provide expected pricing delta for customer-managed keys (ETA: Tue 4/14).
4) HydraHealth: confirm whether they require HSM-backed keys or if cloud KMS (with BYOK) is acceptable (ETA: Mon 4/13).

Notes / clarifications:
- On KMS: Redwood supports BYOK for Dedicated and Private deployments; full HSM integrations are possible but require slightly longer setup and a short validation window. Monica will include a short doc describing both options with the logging sample.
- On logging: the sample export contains structured JSON access logs and a separate KV-cache-prefetch trace. We recommended they validate retention via the sample readme.
- On migration: moving from Hosted to Private typically involves a brief data sync window; planned migrations have been completed with less than two hours of observable interruption for API traffic in our last runbooks, but we recommended a test cutover.

Related attachments shared in Drive: SOC2_report_redwood_2025.pdf, redwood_architecture_diagram_v2.png, sample-logging-export-202603.zip

Next sync: (optional) deep-dive on KMS + migration plan — proposed week of 4/20.

Thanks again — we'll update the Drive folder and tag action items in the HubSpot deal.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Senior Trust & Safety Engineer
Redwood Inference
